newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta quiet after weekend campaign violence.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta quiet after weekend campaign violence.

text.p: The Indonesian capital Jakarta was quiet on Monday after a weekend of clashes in the city between rival partisans campaigning for the May 29 elections, witnesses said.
They said shops and business opened and the streets were jammed with the usual mornign rush-hour traffic jams.

On Saturday and Sunday, clashes between supporters of the ruling Golkar party and loyalists of the minority United Development Party (PPP) broke out in various parts of the capital of 10 million people.
Newspapers also said there was sporadic violence on Sunday in the ancient city of Yogyakarta and the nearby town of Bantul, but there were no injuries or arrests.
Jakarta police chief, Major-General Hamami Nata, said the situation was under control. There were no reports of arrests or injuries.

The three parties entitled to contest the general elections, Golkar, the PPP and the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) issued a statement on Sunday night saying they would hold no more mass rallies in the capital.
